Adelaide, Australia - In a testament to the thriving soccer scene in South Australia, local talent Scott Tunbridge has been making waves with his impressive performances for the North Eastern MetroStars. According to sources close to the team, Tunbridge has been an integral part of the MetroStars' squad, bringing his unique blend of skill and determination to the pitch. "Scott has been a fantastic addition to our team," said MetroStars coach, Michael Barnett. "His work rate and commitment to the team's success have been outstanding, and we're thrilled to have him on board." Data from the National Premier Leagues South Australia (NPL SA) confirms Tunbridge's involvement with the MetroStars. According to the league's official statistics, Tunbridge has made 15 appearances for the team this season, scoring 5 goals and providing 3 assists. Tunbridge's impressive form has not gone unnoticed, with fans and pundits alike praising his contributions to the team's success. "Scott's been a revelation for us this season," said MetroStars fan, Emily Wilson. "He's got a great attitude and is always giving 110% on the pitch. We're lucky to have him representing our club." The North Eastern MetroStars, founded in 1994, have a rich history in Adelaide's soccer community. With a strong focus on developing local talent, the team has become a breeding ground for young players looking to make their mark on the national stage. Tunbridge's success with the MetroStars is a testament to the team's commitment to nurturing homegrown talent. As the NPL SA season heats up, fans will be eagerly watching to see how Tunbridge and his teammates fare in the competition. In a statement, Tunbridge expressed his gratitude to the MetroStars and his excitement for the season ahead. "I'm loving every minute of playing for the MetroStars. The team's been fantastic, and I'm proud to be a part of it. We've got a great squad and I'm confident we can make a real impact in the league this season."

"relevant": false if the document is about some other topic and is of no use for the question; then "cards" is [].
"cards": one card for each answer the document itself gives to the question. Usually that is one card. It is several cards if the document gives several answers, such as a list of names: one card each. It is [] if the document gives no answer. The question may fit several things that share a name: whichever of them this document is about, report its answer. If the document only says that some answer is wrong, write no card for that answer.

The fields of a card:
- "entity": who or what this answer is about, as specifically as the document identifies it: the full name, plus the details the document gives that tell it apart from others with the same name (what kind of thing it is, profession or role, nationality or place, years, creator, other names), even where the question does not ask about them. At most about 25 words.
- "sense": which event, edition, version, condition, place or measure the answer refers to, if the document says; otherwise "not stated".
- "answer": the answer, copied from the document as it is written there, and short: a full name, a date, a number with its unit, or a short phrase. For a yes-or-no question, "yes" or "no".
- "as_of": the date at which this was true, if the document says; otherwise "not stated".
- "claim_kind": "factual", or "opinion" for a judgment, a recommendation or a contested finding.
- "attributed_to": who or what the document says this comes from, such as a census, a study or a named person, if it says; otherwise "not stated".
- "evidence": the sentence of the document that gives the answer, copied word for word. Two sentences if one is not enough.
- "claim": one sentence that states the answer on its own and names the entity.

Inside a JSON string, write a double quote as \".
